mission: Inside the facility's data core. Desh jury-rigs a coupler to thousand-year-old storage. The star map resolves into a network of installations — the Ruusan Corridor — arranged in a perimeter pattern around a central fortress. Ben copies coordinates.
why_now: The warning message is only two words. The data core is where the scope of the problem becomes legible. The scale Ben has been reading alone stops being survey-sized.
conflict: The data is fragmentary — enough to show that something is contained, not enough to say what. The longer Ben reads, the smaller his original assignment looks, and Luke's chain of command is still expecting a standard report.
turning_point: The navigation data includes a route — the Corridor — connecting multiple installations in a perimeter pattern around a central fortress. This is not one facility; it is a network.
opening_hook: Desh pries open a corroded access panel and jams a modern data coupler into storage media older than the Galactic Alliance — the connection sparks twice before holding
closing_hook: Coordinates resolve on the nav computer. The destination is deep in uncharted space — no hyperspace lane, no Republic survey, nothing. Something was deliberately hidden there.
emotional_trajectory: Analytical focus -> dawning scope -> the weight of decision

stakes.personal: Ben's growing investment — this is becoming his mission, not Luke's survey
stakes.interpersonal: Desh raises the professional question: do they report this and wait for backup?
stakes.external: A thousand-year-old containment system is failing and nobody knows

setting: Inside the perimeter facility — data core room, emergency lighting, ancient consoles
sensory_details: Flickering holographic displays showing star maps that do not match modern charts; the hum of ancient power cells; cold enough that Ben's breath catches visible; the Force here has a quality of recording, as if the walls remember who walked these corridors
canon_elements_needed: Pre-Ruusan Jedi military command structure and ranks
Ancient hyperspace navigation charts and star mapping
Jedi containment and monitoring system architecture
Ruusan Corridor and Outer Rim strategic geography
Ancient data storage media in Star Wars Legends
action_beats: Desh pries open a corroded access panel and rigs a modern data coupler to ancient storage media
Holographic star maps flicker to life showing the Ruusan Corridor network — multiple installations in a perimeter pattern
Ben copies the fortress coordinates and route data onto the Steady Returns nav computer
notes: Desh's intelligence training kicks in — he reads the installation as military infrastructure and recognises a command-and-control architecture. His professional assessment carries weight Ben respects. First mention of Gavran's name — a signature on a monitoring log or an authorization line, never a formal introduction. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should read the network without constructing a theory about its builders in this scene. He copies the coordinates; interpretation waits for later. Keep Force-perception register consistent with Ch3 sc1 — pressure rather than pitch or navigation metaphor.
